review: Independent current-SHA closure of five JOS context proposals (Joseph collective and individual are separate variants). This assesses primary-text grounding, reader-facing facts/gates, source IDs, and distinct base-profile integration issues; no draft/proposal files edited.
scope: Current primary WEB and exact source IDs read from pinned local witness and current proposal files. Wikipedia status was rechecked from the recorded readArticle evidence, not newly fetched during this closure.
sourceIDResolution: All current fact/profile source IDs referenced by the five variants resolve to source objects. In particular, the formerly missing JOS 16:1 and 18:5 IDs are now present for facts that summarize those verses; Joseph’s JOS 17:17 fact no longer claims 17:18 content.

records.basisJa: JOS 24:4 explicitly names Jacob alongside Esau and says Jacob and his children went down to Egypt. The individual context begins at 24:4; the 24:32 purchase fact is correctly gated at 24:32 and supported by its exact source ID. This cleanly separates the personal use from the children-of-Israel collective use in 24:32.
records.integrationNoteJa: No known base-profile variant issue relevant to this proposal; root integration still pending by proposal status.

primaryWitnesses.text: I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I gave to Esau Mount Seir, to possess it. Jacob and his children went down into Egypt.

They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver. They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

records.context: collective / ヨセフの子ら（ヨセフの家）
records.basisJa: The collective context first appears at 14:4, and passages identify children/house of Joseph as the Ephraim-Manasseh collective. Facts are gated at 16:4, 17:17, 18:11, and 24:32. The 17:17 fact now stops before 17:18; source IDs include both verses for facts summarizing both. The individual context begins at 17:1 with Joseph as Manasseh’s father and gates the burial fact at 24:32. This resolves the earlier 17:18 look-ahead and missing-source-ID issues.
records.integrationNoteJa: The separate individual/collective schema remains proposed pending root integration.

primaryWitnesses.text: For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and for their property.
The lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
The children of Joseph spoke to Joshua, saying, “Why have you given me just one lot and one part for an inheritance, since we are a numerous people, because the LORD has blessed us so far?”

The children of Joseph said, “The hill country is not enough for us. All the Canaanites who dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both those who are in Beth Shean and its towns, and those who are in the valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph, that is, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, “You are a numerous people, and have great power. You shall not have one lot only;

but the hill country shall be yours. Although it is a forest, you shall cut it down, and it’s farthest extent shall be yours; for you shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong.”
They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall live in his borders on the south, and the house of Joseph shall live in their borders on the north.
The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families. The border of their lot went out between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.

They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver. They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

primaryWitnesses.text: This was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. As for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

So this was for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: for the children of Abiezer, for the children of Helek, for the children of Asriel, for the children of Shechem, for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida. These were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their families.

They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver. They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

records.basisJa: The context split is justified: JOS 13:31 directly says Machir is son of Manasseh; 17:1–3 identify Manasseh personally in the genealogy. But the current individual fact for 17:2 reverses the relationship: it says “マナセの子ヨセフ” (“Joseph, son of Manasseh”), while WEB says “Manasseh the son of Joseph.” Correct the Japanese fact before accepting this proposal. All current fact source IDs resolve to the corresponding WEB verses.
records.integrationNoteJa: Separately, the base collective profile still has 17:3, which is genealogy only, not a collective/territorial use. Root integration must remove 17:3 from collective passages. This base-profile issue is distinct from the proposal’s factual error; JOS 17:1–2 contain both tribal and individual references, so retaining both contexts there is appropriate.

primaryWitnesses.text: Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.

This was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph. As for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

So this was for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: for the children of Abiezer, for the children of Helek, for the children of Asriel, for the children of Shechem, for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida. These were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

records.context: person / ルベン（ボハンの父）
records.basisJa: JOS 15:6 and 18:17 both say “the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben”; they support a Reuben named as Bohan’s father but do not establish him as the eponymous patriarch. The proposal correctly uses unidentified-eponym, states the uncertainty in visible text, and gates the second occurrence as a fact at 18:17. The cited source IDs resolve to the matching verses. Wikipedia is only a related-section link with identityVerified false and relationVerified true; it supports the article-level relation, not identity.
records.integrationNoteJa: Separately, the base Reuben-collective profile still includes 15:6 and 18:17 as passages/facts. These are Bohan’s father, not the Reubenite collective; root integration must remove those from the collective base and retain them only in the cautious eponym context.

primaryWitnesses.text: The border went up to Beth Hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth Arabah; and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
It extended northward, went out at En Shemesh, and went out to Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim. It went down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
